newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jewish settlement to begin next week - Israel.
newsitem.headline: Jewish settlement to begin next week - Israel.

text.p: Israel will begin next week breaking ground for a new Jewish settlement, crux of a deepening crisis with the Palestinians over Arab East Jerusalem, an Israeli cabinet minister said on Wednesday.

Internal Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani told army radio he had discussed the issue with Benjamin Netanyahu on the prime minister's return Wednesday night from a visit to Russia. "We agreed between us that next week the work will begin on Har Homa," Kahalani said.
Earlier on Wednesday, Jordan's King Hussein warned there was a "very strong chance of violence" if Netanyahu pushed ahead with plans for the settlement on the outskirts of East Jerusalem.

Israeli-Palestinian relations -- which warmed briefly after the Jewish state pulled its troops from most of the West Bank town of Hebron in January under a peace deal -- have plunged into turmoil over recent Israeli decisions, notably approval last month of 6,500 new houses for Jews in the holy city's Arab half.
Asked by the radio if bulldozers would arrive at the site next week, Kahalani said, referring to a large Caterpillar tractor: "The order has gone out to a D-9 to begin to move."
Faisal Husseini, head of Palestinian affairs for the Palestinian Authority, has said Palestinians would block bulldozers with their bodies if Israel tried to begin work.
In New York the United Nations General Assembly began a debate expected to end in overwhelming support for a demand that Israel abandon its plans to build on the site.

PLO U.N. observer Nasser al-Kidwa opened debate in the 185-member assembly after the United States on Friday vetoed a Security Council resolution calling on Israel to abandon a project to build on a wooded hill called Har Homa by Israel and Jabal Abu Ghneim by Palestinians.
Israel considers Jerusalem its undivided capital while the Palestinians see East Jerusalem, captured by the Jewish state in the 1967 Middle East war, as the capital of a future Palestinian state.
